items.q: What is Pind Daan and why is Gaya the most sacred place for it?
items.a: Pind Daan is the Vedic ritual of offering rice balls (pindas) to departed ancestors, performed to grant them moksha (liberation). Gaya is the only place in Hindu scripture (Vishnu Purana, Vayu Purana) specifically designated for Pind Daan — Lord Vishnu himself ordained Gaya as the Pitru Tirth (ancestral pilgrimage). Performing Pind Daan here is believed to liberate 7 generations of ancestors.

items.q: How do I book a Pind Daan ceremony?
items.a: Send your ancestor's name, gotra, preferred dates, and number of family members via WhatsApp to +91 84344 57228 or fill our contact form. A coordinator confirms within 4 hours.

items.q: Can NRIs from abroad perform Pind Daan?
items.a: Yes. Pitraya Rituals serves NRI families from the USA, UK, Canada, UAE, Singapore, and Australia. We offer full ceremony coordination, proxy Pind Daan, and live video streaming for families who cannot travel.

items.q: Can daughters perform Pind Daan for their parents?
items.a: Yes. According to Dharmashastra and the Skanda Purana, daughters (putri) can perform Pind Daan and Shradh when there is no son. This is widely practised and fully accepted in Gaya. Our Pandits are well-versed in this tradition.

items.q: What is the best time to perform Pind Daan in Gaya?
items.a: Pind Daan can be performed any day of the year at Gaya. However, Pitru Paksha (the 16-day Hindu lunar period in September/October) is the most auspicious time. Amavasya (new moon) days are also highly auspicious throughout the year.

items.q: What does a complete Pitraya package include?
items.a: All packages include: verified Gayawal Pandit, full ritual Samagri (ceremony materials), hotel accommodation, local transport, Vishnupad Temple darshan coordination, Phalgu River ceremony, Akshayavat visit, and a digital ceremony record.
